text:
[title] Why serving is hard
[body] Every request grows a KV-cache as it generates tokens
[body] Fragmented memory wastes GPU capacity
[body] Tail latency (p99) is what users feel

novice.takeaway: The slide lists key technical challenges—growing memory usage, wasted GPU capacity, and slow worst-case response times—that make serving AI models difficult.
questions: How do these problems connect to the 2.4x speedup?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to understand these specific technical obstacles before explaining their solution.

peer.takeaway: Serving large language models is challenging due to growing memory needs per request, inefficient memory use, and the importance of tail latency for user experience.
questions: What exactly is a KV-cache in this context?
How does memory fragmentation specifically waste GPU capacity?
Why is p99 latency the key metric versus other percentiles?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to understand these three factors as the core challenges their system's improvement addresses.

expert.takeaway: The slide lists core challenges in LLM serving—growing KV-cache, memory fragmentation, and tail latency—that motivate the system introduced in slide 1.
questions: Does fragmentation refer to PagedAttention-style memory management issues?
Is the 2.4x goodput gain achieved by addressing all three listed problems?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants the audience to accept these three issues as the key motivating problems their system solves.
